newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly lower.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly lower on Monday as traders holding short positions tried to push prices down.
The most actively traded January 1998 contract ended at 3,340 yuan ($403), shedding two yuan from Friday's close.
It hit an intra-day high of 3,363 at mid-session and a low of 3,330 in late trading.
The July 1997 contract edged up two yuan to 3,250 and September rose 13 yuan to 3,344. November fell 79 yuan to 3,296 and the March 1998 contract fell 97 to 3,257.
Combined volume fell to 14,600 tonnes from 18,100.
"Some big short-position holders moved into the market to squeeze prices lower late in the session," said a trader.

Traders said the key November contract hit its short-term support level at 3,300 yuan per tonne in late trading. Technical charts showed soybean prices would start a downward trend if the support level was broken on Tuesday.
